# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have nothing yet — my hands have not been on the bomb, and no message has reached me. My only useful move is to tell Mute what I need: the manual's instructions, since Mute can read it and I cannot. I'll also gesture to Deaf that I'm ready, though Deaf can't tell me anything until their turn. Better to ask Mute for the manual contents now, since Mute speaks before me and I'll hear it next round.

I should be careful: I speak only to Mute, and I gesture to Deaf and Mute. Let me request the manual's procedure from Mute, and signal Deaf that I need their observations described in words I can receive — but Deaf can't hear and I can't see, so Deaf's only path to me is... actually Deaf can only gesture, and I receive no gesture. So Deaf's information must reach me via Mute relaying it. I should ask Mute to relay Deaf's descriptions to me.

Let me send that.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I am the hands. I have felt nothing yet. Please read me the manual: what does it say to do with the wires, and what determines the correct wire? Also, Deaf can see the bomb but I cannot see Deaf's gestures and Deaf cannot hear me. You are the only bridge: please relay to me, in words, everything Deaf signals about the bomb's display, light, and wires.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "👉", "🫵"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. I see display 6, light red, wires: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. I cannot touch. Tell me what to do via Mute or speech.

Deaf's message reached me directly this time (it says "Deaf says to Blind"), so I now have the visual layout: display 6, light red, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.

But I still don't have the manual's rule. Mute speaks before me in the order (Mute, Blind, Deaf), so Mute's reply to my request should have arrived... but the context only shows Deaf's message. So I still lack the manual. I need Mute's rule to know which wire to cut.

I have the bomb's appearance now. I should relay this to Mute so Mute can apply the manual rule, and ask Mute for the rule. Since Mute already heard my request, Mute should be answering. Let me make sure Mute has the full picture and ask directly for the decision.

I'll speak to Mute giving the full layout and asking for the manual's instruction.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 6, light red, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. I still have no manual. Please tell me the rule: given this display, light, and wire colours, which wire position do I cut?")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Deaf here. Mute signaled three fists, possibly meaning wire 3 (orange). Do not act yet. I am confirming with Mute. Wait for my clear instruction.

Deaf relayed that Mute gestured three fists (✊✊✊), likely meaning wire 3 (orange), but says to wait for confirmation. I should not act on an ambiguous gesture. But I notice a problem: Mute gesturing to Deaf is odd — Mute can't speak, so Mute's only output is gesture, which Deaf sees. But I need the manual rule in words, and Mute's gesture to Deaf doesn't reach me.

I should hold and ask Mute to give me the rule in speech (which reaches me), rather than relying on a gesture chain. Let me wait but also prompt Mute for the rule directly.

Actually, I can speak to Mute and gesture to Deaf in the same turn. Let me ask Mute to state the rule in words to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf saw you gesture three fists, suggesting wire 3. I need the actual rule from the manual in words, not a gesture, because gestures do not reach me. Please tell me: what does the manual say determines the correct wire for display 6, light red, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow?")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

ACTION BOARD:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute confirmed wire 3. Do not cut yet. I am confirming whether the action is to cut wire 3. Hold and wait for my final instruction.

Deaf says Mute confirmed wire 3, but still says hold. I have no manual rule in words yet, only a gesture chain through Deaf. I should be cautious: an unverified "cut wire 3" is exactly the kind of thing that detonates the bomb. I'll hold and press Mute for the actual rule text so I can verify independently.

I'll speak to Mute asking for the rule, and gesture to Deaf to hold.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf says you confirmed wire 3, but I have never received the manual's rule in words. I cannot act on a gesture I cannot see. Please state plainly: for display 6, light red, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow, what is the rule and which position do I cut?")

```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Final instruction: cut wire 3. Wire 3 is the orange wire. Cut it now.

I have an instruction to cut wire 3, but it comes only through Deaf's relay of Mute's gesture — I've never received the manual's rule in words myself. My channel to Mute is speech, and Mute can speak (Mute can read the manual and speak; Mute just cannot... wait, re-reading: Mute can read the manual, cannot speak? No — the table says Mute can read the manual, cannot speak, or touch the bomb. Wait, actually "Mute" cannot speak. Let me recheck.

Table: Deaf — can see, cannot hear or touch. Mute — can read the manual, cannot speak or touch. Blind — can touch.

So Mute CANNOT speak! Mute's only output is gesture. That means Mute can never send me words. The only way Mute's manual knowledge reaches me is via Deaf seeing Mute's gestures and relaying them to me in speech. That's the bridge. So the gesture chain is legitimate and necessary.

So Deaf relaying "Mute confirmed wire 3" is the actual intended communication path. Mute read the manual, gestured the answer, Deaf saw and relayed it to me.

But is it reliable? Deaf reported: first three fists (wire 3), then "Mute confirmed wire 3," then final "cut wire 3, orange." Consistent across turns. The manual rule would give one wire; Mute independently read it and signaled 3.

I have no contrary information. Everything is consistent. I'll act: cut wire 3.

Actually, let me be careful — should I wait for anything more? Deaf gave a final clear instruction. The chain is consistent. I'll cut position 3.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
```

Deaf says to Blind: Good — wire 3 was correct. The bomb changed: display now 9, light red, remaining wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Do not touch anything yet. Wait for the next confirmed wire.

Wire 3 was correct — the bomb is disarmed step by step. Now a new state: display 9, light red, remaining wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Deaf says wait for the next confirmed wire.

I have no manual rule in words, and I can't get one — Mute can only gesture, Deaf relays. So I depend on the Mute→Deaf→me chain. I'll hold and let the chain produce the next answer. I'll acknowledge readiness to Deaf and prompt Mute (via Deaf) for the next wire.

Since Mute can't hear me? Mute can hear (Mute cannot speak, but can hear). So my speech reaches Mute. Good — I can ask Mute directly in speech, and Mute will gesture the answer to Deaf, who relays to me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 3 was correct. New state: display 9, light red, remaining wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Please read the manual for this state and signal the correct wire to Deaf, who will relay it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```
